docs.title: Corio
docs.text:
Corio is a practical Python toolkit for building small services, automation, data pipelines, and AI/ML support code without re-solving the same project plumbing every time.

It bundles the pieces that tend to sit between "standard library" and "application code": typed paths with serialization helpers, pydantic-friendly data models, CLI settings, structured logging spans, iterator progress, FastAPI/MCP endpoint scaffolding, release metadata generation, test environment generation, and opt-in integrations for docs, Docker, search, tabular data, PDFs, OpenAI, Home Assistant, DNS, caching, encryption, and more.

Corio is organized as one package with optional extras. Install the small core by default, then opt into the heavier tools a project actually needs.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install corio

Examples:

pip install "corio[api]"
pip install "corio[tabular]"
pip install "corio[db.search]"
pip install "corio[infra]"

docs.title: Why Use It
docs.text:
• Use paths as real application objects. Read and write JSON, YAML, TOML, text, and derived paths directly from corio.Path.
  • Make CLIs from typed models. Corio builds on pydantic settings patterns so small tools can stay declarative.
  • Wrap iteration with observability. corio.iterator.Iterator tracks count, percentage, elapsed time, ETA, completion, and cleanup.
  • Expose tools as HTTP and MCP endpoints. Define endpoint classes once and mount them into FastAPI and MCP surfaces.
  • Keep release metadata generated. corio pyproject turns Corio dependency groups and project metadata into the generated pyproject.toml sections.
  • Configure generated test environments. Set test_pass_env in Corio metadata to pass selected environment variables through every generated tox test environment.
  • Install integrations only when needed. Extras keep heavy dependencies like API servers, vector search, ML, PDFs, and tabular tooling out of the base install.

docs.title: Typed Paths And Data Files
docs.text:
from corio import Path

path = Path("runs/latest/config.yaml")
path.parent.mkdirf()
path.write_data({
    "model": "embedder-v2",
    "batch_size": 64,
})

config = path.read_data()
json_path = path.get_conversion_path("json")
json_path.parent.mkdirf()
json_path.write_data(config)

docs.title: Observable Iteration
docs.text:
from corio.iterator import Iterator

documents = [{"id": "a"}, {"id": "b"}, {"id": "c"}]

for document in Iterator(documents):
    # Work happens inside per-item logging spans with progress stats.
    process(document)

The iterator tracks count, total, percentage, elapsed time, rate, ETA, completion logs, and closes the wrapped iterator when possible.

docs.title: FastAPI And MCP Tools
docs.text:
from functools import cached_property

from corio import api


class Search(api.endpoint.API):
    """Search indexed documents."""

    PATH = "/search"
    TAGS = "documents"

    async def run(self, query: str):
        return {"query": query, "results": []}


class Reindex(api.endpoint.Tool):
    """Rebuild the document index."""

    async def run(self):
        return {"status": "queued"}


class Service(api.Base):
    TITLE = "Document Service"
    PORT = 8080

    @cached_property
    def ENDPOINTS(self):
        return [Search, Reindex]


Service().launch()

The same endpoint model can feed HTTP routes and MCP tools, so internal automation and external APIs stay aligned.

docs.title: Project Metadata
docs.text:
Corio projects keep dependency intent in [tool.corio.dependencies]; generated package metadata lives in [project.optional-dependencies].

[tool.corio.dependencies]
semantic = ["sentence_transformers", "metrics"]
metrics = ["tabular", "ranx"]
tabular = ["pandas", "tabulate", "openpyxl", "odfpy", "deepdiff"]

Then regenerate:

corio pyproject

That keeps extras flattened for packaging while preserving a maintainable source-of-truth dependency graph.

docs.title: Async CLI Execution
docs.text: Typed CLI models expose an async run() method. Synchronous entrypoints can use launch(), while applications that already run an event loop can await run() directly. Subcommand dispatch supports both synchronous and asynchronous command implementations.

docs.title: Useful Areas
docs.text:
• corio.path: typed path helpers, app paths, file type guessing, serialization helpers.
  • corio.dm and corio.sets: pydantic-oriented models and settings/CLI support.
  • corio.api: FastAPI and MCP endpoint composition.
  • corio.iterator: progress-aware iterable wrapper and small collection helpers.
  • corio.infra: release, docs, tox, and pyproject generation tooling.
  • corio.db.search: vector search helpers around qdrant and embeddings.
  • corio.tabular, corio.semantic, corio.metric: data and retrieval metrics helpers.
  • corio.encrypt, corio.sec: project secret and encryption workflows.
  • corio.ha, corio.dns, corio.mqtt, corio.webhook: operations and home automation integrations.

docs.title: api
docs.text:
from corio import api

api provides a lightweight FastAPI base where endpoints are defined as classes.

Main pieces:

  • endpoint.Base: base endpoint contract (run)
  • endpoint.API: class-based HTTP endpoint with registration helpers
  • endpoint.MCP: class-based MCP endpoint with tool registration helpers
  • endpoint.Tool: MCP tool endpoint
  • endpoint.Prompt: MCP prompt endpoint
  • endpoint.Resource: MCP resource endpoint
  • Base: app bootstrap, endpoint registration, child API mounting, and uvicorn launch helpers

Install:

pip install "corio[api]" --upgrade

docs.title: Typical Endpoint Pattern
docs.text:
from __future__ import annotations

from corio import api


class HealthApi(api.Base):
    TITLE = "Health API"

    @property
    def ENDPOINTS(self):
        return [Health]

    @property
    def TRANSFORMS(self):
        return []


class Health(api.endpoint.API):
    """Service health."""

    PATH = "/health"
    TAGS = "status"

    async def run(self):
        return {"ok": True}

Run with:

HealthApi.launch()

docs.title: Real-World Usage Pattern (generalized)
docs.text:
Sibling repos commonly:

  • subclass api.Base
  • keep endpoint class list in ENDPOINTS (can include api.endpoint.API and api.endpoint.MCP)
  • keep MCP transform class list in TRANSFORMS (each class is initialized with self.mcp)
  • attach tags per feature area (cache, blocking, documents, etc.)
  • mount child APIs using children when composing a larger API surface

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Base instruments FastAPI via corio.logs.
  • In dev mode, exception handling is configured to re-raise for easier debugging.
  • Endpoints register as GET routes.
  • MCP endpoint classes register tools via self.mcp.tool(...).
  • Default endpoint path is /{endpoint_class_name_lower} unless PATH is overridden.

docs.title: Search chunk retrieval
docs.text: corio.db.search.document.Document.get_chunks accepts an optional Qdrant Filter as runtime_filter. Corio ANDs it with the document ID and chunk-index conditions. Use it when several logical collections share one physical Qdrant collection; filtering by the logical collection ID keeps chunk retrieval scoped to the requested collection.

docs.title: dm
docs.text:
from corio import dm

dm provides the data modelling layer built on Pydantic, with utilities aimed at robust parsing and schema ergonomics.

Highlights:

  • Field: reusable field definitions with optional auto-defaulting and title/description templating
  • Base: model base that can aggregate FIELDS declarations across inheritance
  • to_df: quick conversion to tabular representation (tabular extra needed there)

Install:

pip install "corio[dm]" --upgrade

docs.title: Typical Model Pattern
docs.text:
from corio import dm


class User(dm.Base):
    id: int
    name: str


user = User.model_validate_json('{"id": 1, "name": "Ada"}')

docs.title: Field Class Pattern
docs.text:
dm.Field is useful when you want reusable field components across multiple models:

from corio import dm


class FieldName(dm.Field):
    ANNOTATION = str
    DESCRIPTION = "Human-readable user name."


class User(dm.Base):
    FIELDS = [FieldName]
    id: int

docs.title: CLI Integration
docs.text: dm.Base provides data modelling without CLI execution. For settings and CLI subcommands, use the dedicated bases in sets: sets.Base for a CLI entrypoint and sets.SubCommand for models that dispatch nested commands.

docs.title: dns
docs.text:
from corio import dns

dns contains a small DNS toolkit for building resolvers/proxies, with request/response datamodels and plain or DoH upstream clients.

Main parts:

  • dns.dm: exchange/request/response models (Exchange, Request, Response)
  • dns.client: upstream clients (Plain, HTTP)
  • dns.server: async UDP server base with caching and structured handling
  • dns.proxy: proxy server base that lets you hook process_question and process_upstream

Install:

pip install "corio[dns]" --upgrade

docs.title: Request Flow
docs.text:
The base dns.proxy.Proxy model is stage-based:

  1. process_question(exchange) - mutate/short-circuit before upstream.
  2. upstream resolve (dns.client.Plain or dns.client.HTTP).
  3. process_upstream(exchange) - inspect/replace upstream answers.
  4. finalize(exchange) - finalize message and completion state.

dns.server.Plain handles UDP datagrams, cache check/write, reverse lookup context, and response send.

from corio import dns


class PolicyProxy(dns.proxy.Proxy):
    def process_question(self, exchange):
        # rewrite or block before upstream
        return

    def process_upstream(self, exchange):
        # inspect upstream answers, optionally block
        return

docs.title: Upstream Selection
docs.text: dns.client.HTTP is used for DoH, and can be selected dynamically by wrapping clients in a rule-driven selector (for example via patterns.Transformer subclasses).

docs.title: Data Model Objects
docs.text:
• dns.dm.Request: parsed question and helper metadata.
  • dns.dm.Response: response/message wrapper with rcode, ttl, answer access.
  • dns.dm.Exchange: mutable exchange state from ingress to final response.

docs.title: encrypt
docs.text:
from corio import encrypt

encrypt provides AGE-based encryption helpers for serializable Python data.

Classes:

  • Encryptor: encrypt/decrypt full payloads
  • EncryptorValues: tree transform that encrypts/decrypts leaf values
  • EncryptorValuesSelect: selective node encryption using path-match patterns

Install:

pip install "corio[encrypt]" --upgrade

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
• Values are serialized to JSON before encryption.
  • Cipher payloads are wrapped in a recognizable header marker.
  • EncryptorValues* preserves tree structure and only transforms leaves.

docs.title: Example: Selective Node Encryption
docs.text:
from corio import encrypt

data = {
    "service": {"token": "abc", "region": "eu"},
    "db": {"password": "secret", "port": 5432},
}

enc = encrypt.EncryptorValuesSelect(nodes=["service/token", "db/password"])
cipher = enc.encrypt(data)
plain = enc.decrypt(cipher)

nodes accepts path-style match expressions evaluated against leaf nodes.

By default the key is read from the FMTR_AGE_KEY environment variable.

docs.title: infra
docs.text:
from corio import infra

infra is the release/build orchestration layer used by corio projects.

Core objects:

  • Project: package metadata + runtime release context
  • Repository: git operations (fetch, tagging, push flow)
  • Stack: container build/deploy definitions (development and production variants)
  • Releaser: version increment, package build/upload, docs deploy flow
  • infrastructure.api.Api: FastAPI surface for release/build/recreate operations

Production images built by Stack run their entrypoint as the unprivileged user account (UID 1000). Files accessed by the process must be readable or writable by that UID as needed.

The production container CLI defaults to podman. Set container_cli when a project needs a different compatible CLI. A configured container_host enables production image builds during the release flow and identifies the remote container host:

[tool.corio.metadata]
container_cli = "podman"
container_host = "ssh://user@host"

The host is passed directly to the configured container client, so an SSH endpoint can be used without a CLI context. The build log reports the configured container target.

Install:

pip install "corio[infra]" --upgrade

docs.title: Typical Usage
docs.text:
from corio import infra

project = infra.Project("corio")
project.releaser.run(release=True)

The same release flow is available from the command line:

corio infra release --name corio

docs.title: API Usage
docs.text:
infra.Api exposes release/build/recreate endpoints and is used by infra wrapper repos:

from corio import infra

infra.Api.launch()

docs.title: Docs Release Expectations
docs.text:
Docs release expects:

  • docs/ content in repo root
  • tool.corio.metadata.docs.nav in pyproject.toml

ReleaseDocumentation builds MkDocs configuration dynamically from project metadata, so nav structure in pyproject is part of the release contract.

docs.title: Generated Test Environments
docs.text:
Before running tests, the release workflow generates tox environments from the package's test files and dependency metadata. By default, it creates one development environment (dev) and one production environment (prod) for the full test suite. Set test_envs = true under [tool.corio.metadata] to generate environments for each package module with a matching tests/test_<module>.py file instead:

[tool.corio.metadata]
test_envs = true

Per-module environments are named <module>.dev and <module>.prod. Development environments use the source checkout and local editable dependencies; production environments install the package. The generated production environments make up tox's default env_list, which is what the release workflow runs. Development environment names are recorded in [tool.corio.test-envs].dev for source-tree testing.

docs.title: Release Flow (high-level)
docs.text:
releaser.run(...) orchestrates:

  1. increment the version and generate pyproject.toml release metadata used by tests
  2. run configured tox tests, retrying dependency-resolution failures for up to 10 minutes
  3. after tests pass, update add-on and changelog release metadata
  4. commit, tag, and push
  5. optional container build/push
  6. package build/upload
  7. docs deploy
  8. remove generated release artifacts from the worktree, including build/test caches, coverage data, and Python bytecode caches; coverage configuration is preserved

Test failures block both stable and pre-releases. On failure, the generated pyproject.toml is restored; add-on and changelog updates have not yet run. The release changes are staged only after all incrementors succeed.

The release-start log message names the project and the Corio runtime version used.

If tox fails with No solution found when resolving dependencies, the release retries tox every 10 seconds for up to 10 minutes. Other dependency-installation failures and test failures stop the release immediately.

When a current pre-release version has no matching Git tag, the release flow stops rather than assuming that version can be safely reused. Resolve the release state or pin the intended stable base explicitly before retrying.

docs.title: interface
docs.text:
from corio import interface

interface is a thin base for Flet UI apps with lifecycle hooks, typed context wiring, and web-app identity defaults.

Main pieces:

  • Context: typed runtime container around flet.Page
  • Base: ft.Column subclass with an async constructor (new), routing hooks, identity metadata, and a launch helper
  • decorators update and progress for post-action page refresh/progress display

Install:

pip install "corio[interface]" --upgrade

docs.title: Typical Base Pattern
docs.text:
import flet as ft

from corio import function, interface


class SampleApp(interface.Base[interface.Context]):
    @function.ccp
    def metadata(cls) -> interface.Metadata:
        """

        Return the sample app's manifest metadata.

        """
        return interface.Metadata(
            name="Sample Studio",
            short_name="Studio",
            description="An example Flet web application.",
            theme_color="#224466",
            background_color="#F0F2F4",
        )

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(controls=[ft.Text(self.metadata.name)])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    SampleApp.launch()

Base.metadata is an @ccp that returns a typed Metadata model. Metadata.name is required; Base supplies the interface class name by default. The optional short_name is an abbreviated label browsers may use where the full name does not fit; omit it to let the browser use name. See the manifest definitions of name and short_name. The model also defines Flet's manifest defaults, including icon entries and the theme_color and background_color fields. Override the property to customize the complete manifest; use ManifestIcon for typed icon entries, or subclass Metadata to add application-specific fields.

Before launch, Base.prep_assets() creates PATH_ASSETS and writes manifest.json there through Corio's Path.write_json(). Its default is corio.paths.paths.assets / "interface"; override PATH_ASSETS when an application needs another directory. The method returns nothing—Base.launch() passes PATH_ASSETS directly to Flet. This model is the source of truth: a previous manifest is replaced at startup, so declare custom fields and icon lists in the metadata override. The directory must be writable while the app starts.

Flet serves files in the assets directory over its bundled web assets. Put custom files under PATH_ASSETS at these exact, case-sensitive paths (relative to that directory) to replace the defaults:

Asset path Used for favicon.png Browser-tab favicon icons/loading-animation.png Dynamic web app loading image, shown until Flutter draws its first frame icons/icon-192.png, icons/icon-512.png PWA icons icons/icon-maskable-192.png, icons/icon-maskable-512.png Maskable Android PWA icons icons/apple-touch-icon-192.png iOS “Add to Home Screen” icon

Flet serves a matching file as-is; supply the intended dimensions and maskable artwork yourself. The default Metadata model references the standard Flet icon paths. Override metadata to choose different paths; those files must be present under PATH_ASSETS.

Loading image versus PWA splash screen

icons/loading-animation.png replaces the dynamic website's pre-first-frame loading image; it is not a full-screen splash configuration. An installed PWA's launch splash is generated by the browser/platform from its manifest, icons, and colors. For flet build web, Flet has a separate build-time splash-screen configuration (assets/splash.png or assets/splash.svg).

Base.launch() targets Flet's dynamic runtime. For flet build web, configure build-time identity in [tool.flet] (product, description) and [tool.flet.web] (pwa_short_name, pwa_theme_color, pwa_background_color); build splash settings are separate from the dynamic loading image. See Flet's dynamic web publishing guide, asset guide, and build configuration.

docs.title: Advanced Pattern
docs.text:
• Override async def new(cls, page) for async setup (database/session/bootstrap).
  • Configure PATH_ASSETS and PATH_UPLOADS for static/upload handling.
  • Use tabs/views and route hooks (route, pop) for multi-view apps. Handlers receive Flet events: route(event: ft.RouteChangeEvent) and pop(event: ft.ViewPopEvent); view-pop details are available on event.route, event.view, and event.page.
  • Base auto-manages FLET_SECRET_KEY when missing.
@classmethod
async def new(cls, page):
    # async startup work here
    self = await super().new(page)
    return self

update and progress decorators are useful for callback methods that need guaranteed page refresh and spinner visibility.

docs.title: path
docs.text:
from corio import path

path is one of the core modules in corio. It extends pathlib.Path and provides package-aware path resolution helpers used throughout the rest of the library.

Primary exports:

  • Path: enhanced path object with convenience readers/writers (json, yaml, toml, .env, inferred read_data/write_data)
  • PackagePaths: canonical package/repo metadata and path discovery
  • InvalidCorioRepoError: raised when a path does not identify exactly one Corio package marker
  • AppPaths: appdirs wrapper (path.app extra)

docs.title: What Is Useful Here
docs.text:
• Path.read_data() / Path.write_data(obj) infer serializer by suffix:
  • .json -> JSON
  • .yaml / .yml -> YAML
  • .toml -> TOML
  • .env -> dotenv map
  • unknown -> text
  • Path.find_up(name) walks up parent directories for repo-root style config lookup.
  • Path.mkdirf() is a parents=True, exist_ok=True convenience.
  • PackagePaths().metadata gives strongly-typed access to tool.corio.metadata from package pyproject.
  • WSL absolute Windows paths are auto-converted when running under WSL.

docs.title: Editable packages
docs.text:
Record editable package identifiers in [tool.corio.metadata]:

[tool.corio.metadata]
editables = ["<package-name>"]

PackagePaths().metadata.editables exposes the configured identifiers. When corio pyproject generates a pre-release project's configuration, it sets uv's prerelease policy to if-necessary globally and for each editable package. This prefers stable dependencies while allowing prereleases where required. For stable projects, it removes those generated prerelease settings.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
from corio import Path

path = Path("settings.yaml")
config = path.read_data()  # same as read_yaml() here

out = Path("build/runtime.toml")
out.parent.mkdirf()
out.write_data({"name": "corio", "enabled": True})
runtime = out.read_data()

from corio import PackagePaths

paths = PackagePaths()
print(paths.repo)
print(paths.metadata.version)
print(paths.metadata.description)

from corio import Path

path_secrets = Path.cwd().find_up(".secrets.yml")
print(path_secrets)

docs.title: Serializer Methods
docs.text:
Path also exposes explicit methods when you do not want extension inference:

  • read_json() / write_json()
  • read_yaml() / write_yaml()
  • read_toml() / write_toml()
  • read_env() / write_env()

docs.title: patterns
docs.text:
from corio import patterns

patterns is a regex-driven transformation utility for structured rewrite rules.

Main types:

  • Key: serializable pattern key with named capture support
  • Item: source/target rule pair
  • Transformer: compiles many rules into one expression and applies one-pass or recursive rewrite

Install:

pip install "corio[patterns]" --upgrade

docs.title: Why Use It
docs.text:
Use this when dictionary-style lookups are not enough and you need:

  • regex capture groups
  • templated target rewrites
  • recursive transforms with loop detection

docs.title: Real-world Pattern (generalized)
docs.text:
In DNS tooling, repos use:

  • Key subclasses (name, records)
  • Item rules mapping a source key to transformed key or sentinel value
  • Transformer.get(key) to select upstream behavior or blocklist output

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from corio import patterns


@dataclass
class HostKey(patterns.Key):
    FILLS = {"sub": r"[a-z0-9-]+"}
    host: str


rules = [
    patterns.Item(source=HostKey(host=r"{sub}\.example\.com"), target=HostKey(host=r"edge-{sub}.example.net")),
]

tx = patterns.Transformer(items=rules, default=None)

If recursive mode is enabled and rules loop, RewriteCircularLoopError is raised.

docs.title: secrets
docs.text:
from corio import sec

secrets builds on encrypt + sets to provide repo-oriented secret file workflows.

Main model:

  • Config: reads .secrets.yml, definitions, and contexts
  • Encrypt command: writes encrypted <raw>.black.yml files from <raw>.red.yml files
  • Decrypt command: writes <raw>.red.yml files back from <raw>.black.yml when allowed

Install:

pip install "corio[secrets]" --upgrade

docs.title: High-level behavior
docs.text:
1. Define raw file globs and encrypted nodes in .secrets.yml; the .red.yml suffix is implicit.
  2. Run encrypt mode to produce *.black.yml.
  3. Run decrypt mode for selected contexts when needed.

Any *.red.yml file not covered by a definition is still encrypted. All of its fields are encrypted and a warning is logged.

Encryption deletes each red file by default after its black counterpart has been written or verified. Pass --delete false to retain red files. Decryption writes red files by default; pass --restore true to write each value to its original filename and format instead. Pass --force true to overwrite every target regardless of its age or current contents, and --preserve true to copy the black file's permissions and ownership to the decrypted target.

docs.title: Minimal .secrets.yml shape
docs.text:
contexts:
  - name: web
    files:
      - "services/web/**/*.yml"

definitions:
  - files:
      - "services/web/**/*.yml"
    nodes:
      - "env/password"
      - "env/token"

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
Entry point:

corio secrets encrypt --context=web
corio secrets decrypt --context=web

For example, the definition path services/web/config.yaml matches services/web/config.yaml.red.yml. Encryption writes services/web/config.yaml.black.yml, and decryption restores the red file when the encrypted side is newer or changed.

docs.title: CLI subcommands

sets.SubCommand adds command execution to a dm.Base model. Use it for models that dispatch nested CLI subcommands; ordinary data models can continue to inherit directly from dm.Base. sets.Base already includes this behavior for the CLI entrypoint.

from pydantic_settings import CliSubCommand

docs.title: Shell commands
docs.text: corio.shell provides a small DSL for building command arguments and shell expressions. It is a separate package rather than a corio.__init__ export.

docs.title: Build a command
docs.text:
from corio.shell import arg, ex, val

command = ex.git.status(--arg.short)
print(str(command))  # git status --short
print(command.tokens())  # ['git', 'status', '--short']

Use ex (or its alias, shell) to start a command. Attribute names form command and subcommand names; underscores become hyphens, so ex.some_tool.run_ builds some-tool run. Pass positional strings or expressions to add arguments.

Use arg to build options. A single - or + prefix is added with unary minus or plus; repeat it to build long options. Add a separated value with +, or an equals value with ==. Use val when you want to explicitly represent a value:

output = ex.tool(--arg.output + val.report_file)
mode = ex.tool(--arg.mode == "quiet")

Values are kept as individual tokens. str(command) renders a shell-quoted representation for display, while command.tokens() returns the argument list suitable for process APIs.

docs.title: Combine commands
docs.text:
Use &, ^, and | to build AND, OR, and pipe expressions, respectively. Parenthesize combinations when you need to make the intended grouping explicit:

workflow = ex.prepare() & (ex.verify() | ex.recover())
print(str(workflow))  # prepare && (verify || recover)

Operator expressions render shell syntax. Command expressions can run locally with .run(), which invokes the command using its token list without asking a shell to interpret syntax. A leading + on a command expression is shorthand for .run(). To run a command expression through a shell, pass shell=True; to run a composed operator expression on systems with sh, pass its rendered form to the shell:

ex.sh("-c", str(workflow)).run()

docs.title: Truncation

truncate and truncate_mid flatten multiline text by default. Set flatten_text=False to preserve line breaks while limiting the string length.

When requesting a Truncation result with return_type=Truncation, use was_truncated to distinguish unchanged text from text that was shortened.

from corio import strings

result = strings.truncate(
    "first line\nsecond line",
    length=12,
    flatten_text=False,
    return_type=strings.Truncation,
)

assert result.was_truncated is True
